reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) confirms that high cooling rates in LPBF/SLM inhibit segregation and refine microstructures, but none of the passages specifically address high scanning speeds as the primary control parameter, nor do they provide data on AlCrFeNiSi or directly link scanning speed to reduced residual stress and defect density. The premises are therefore only loosely supported by general AM principles rather than specific prior results.
premises: High scanning speeds in laser AM reduce thermal input and heat-affected zone
Reduced thermal input limits atomic diffusion and compositional segregation
Reduced thermal input lowers residual thermal stresses
Reduced thermal input decreases defect density (porosity, cracking)
These microstructural improvements enhance mechanical integrity (strength, ductility)
